title: The October Revolution, 1917 — the storming that was mostly staged later
sources: Wikipedia: October Revolution — led by Lenin's Bolsheviks; began with an insurrection in Petrograd on 7 November 1917 (25 October in the Julian calendar Russia still used — hence 'October'); the Provisional Government was led by Alexander Kerensky; that night they captured the Winter Palace, seat of the Provisional Government; the cruiser Aurora fired a blank shot from the harbour; the final assault on the palace — against 3,000 cadets, officers, cossacks and female soldiers — was not vigorously resisted; the cadets and the 140 volunteers of the Women's Battalion surrendered rather than resist the 40,000-strong attacking force; the initial stage occurred largely without casualties; a 1920 reenactment, The Storming of the Winter Palace, watched by 100,000 spectators, provided the model for official films showing fierce fighting, although the insurgents had faced little opposition; stills from Sergei Eisenstein's staged film October (1928) came to be taken as truth; 7 November became the Soviet Union's national day
Also on this day (candidates.md, in the app): 1916 Jeannette Rankin becomes the first woman elected to the US Congress; 1861 Ulysses S. Grant's first combat
Archive film (public domain): Sergei Eisenstein and Grigori Aleksandrov, October: Ten Days That Shook the World (1928) — a staged dramatisation

Photos and art (public domain): the Winter Palace after the seizure, 8 November 1917 (Yakov Steinberg); the Gothic Hall after the seizure; the Women's Battalion at the Winter Palace; Lenin, 1920; Lenin speaking, 1917; the July 1917 riot on Nevsky Prospect (Viktor Bulla); the Military Revolutionary Committee proclamation; Boris Kustodiev, The Bolshevik; E. Barnard Lintott, The Attack on the Winter Palace (1917); the cruiser Aurora's gun

post.facebook:
On this day in 1917, Lenin's Bolsheviks took the Winter Palace in Petrograd — the night now called the October Revolution, because Russia still used the old Julian calendar.

The cruiser Aurora fired a single shot from the river: a blank. Inside the palace were about 3,000 defenders — cadets, Cossacks and the Women's Battalion. Outside, some 40,000. The palace was barely defended; most of its defenders surrendered, and the first stage of the revolution went almost without casualties.

The epic "storming" came later. In 1920 it was restaged as a spectacle for 100,000 spectators, and in 1928 Sergei Eisenstein filmed it again for his film October, with fierce fighting that never happened. For decades, stills from that staged film were taken as the truth.

The film clips in our video are from Eisenstein's October — a dramatisation, not news footage.

Also on 7 November: Jeannette Rankin became the first woman elected to the US Congress (1916), and Ulysses S. Grant fought his first battle (1861).

youtube.description:
7 November 1917: the Bolsheviks took the Winter Palace in Petrograd — the October Revolution, named after Russia's old calendar. The cruiser Aurora fired one blank shot; about 3,000 defenders faced 40,000 attackers, and most surrendered with almost no fighting. The dramatic storming came later: a 1920 restaging for 100,000 spectators, then Sergei Eisenstein's 1928 film October — whose staged scenes were taken as the truth for decades.

Also on 7 November: Jeannette Rankin, first woman in Congress (1916), and Grant's first battle (1861).
